blocks.content: This is the most basic case, as Z is the first element to be inserted into the tree.
Since every new insertion has to be a red node, Z is initially red.
Let's see if this new node violates the red-black tree property.
Since Z has invisible black NIL leaves, the leaf property is satisfied.

blocks.alt: Satisfy the Leaf Property with Invisible Black NIL Leaves

blocks.content: This property specifies that the root node must be black. Since Z is a root node but red in color, it violates the root property.
To fix this, we simply change the color to black.

blocks.alt: Change the Color of the Root Node to Black

blocks.content: 3. Red Node Property and Black Depth Property
The red node property and black depth property are both satisfied.
Thus, the solution to this case is quite simple, as all we have to do is color Z black.
